Suggests GRAND TOTAL pattern did not match due to OCR variant ('GrandTotal' with no space) and fallback failed, and that failure was written as '' rather than None."},{"id":"date_034","filename":"034.jpg","field":"date","observed":"2018-08-09","issue":"Date on receipt is '09/03/2018' (DD/MM/YYYY → 2018-03-09), but prediction gave 2018-08-09, indicating the date parser mis-ordered month/day or picked a different numeric triple on the page."},{"id":"schema_null_encoding","filename":"078.jpg","field":"total_amount","observed":"empty string","issue":"Missing extraction was serialized as '' (empty string) instead of a real null cell; this violates the task's 'value is set to null' contract and the xlsx strict-schema guidance in the candidate skill."}],"root_causes":[{"id":"rc_keyword_priority_tiebreak","summary":"Within a priority tier the candidate skill picks the LAST matching line, but final-total lines are not always last: GST-summary rows, 'Incl. of GST' intermediate totals, and OCR-duplicated TOTAL lines can come after the real total. There is no section-aware suppression (e.g. ignore lines after 'GST SUMMARY'/'TAX SUMMARY') and no preference for rounded/grand-total variants when both pre- and post-rounding totals are present.","evidence":["074.jpg picked 'Total incl. of GST 702.00' over 'Total Amt Rounded 102.00'","077.jpg picked 'Total (Inclusive of GST) 23.26' over final 'TOTAL 23.25' after Rounding Adj"]},{"id":"rc_ocr_variant_keywords","summary":"Keyword regexes require clean whitespace/spelling ('GRAND\\s*TOTAL', 'TOTAL\\s*:?\\s*RM', 'NETT?\\s*TOTAL') and do not tolerate common receipt-OCR corruptions: concatenations ('GrandTotal'), letter/digit swaps in RM ('RN','Ri','ARH'), stray punctuation, and 'Total' split across two tokens. When the top-tier keyword fails, the code falls to a weaker tier that matches tax/summary rows.","evidence":["078.jpg 'GrandTotal 92.80' not recognized as GRAND TOTAL","064.jpg/019.jpg 'Total RN/Ri' not recognized as TOTAL RM"]},{"id":"rc_null_serialization","summary":"When extraction fails the writer stores an empty string in the xlsx cell instead of a real null (None/empty cell). The strict-schema section of the candidate xlsx skill already warns about this, but the image-ocr pipeline and the xlsx writing step are not jointly enforcing it.","evidence":["078.jpg total_amount serialized as '' in predictions"]},{"id":"rc_date_format_ambiguity","summary":"Date regex uses a single DD/MM/YYYY-first ordering with no disambiguation when both orderings yield a valid calendar date, and does not anchor on a 'Date:' label. For receipts where the first numeric date-like token on the page is not the transaction date, or where DD and MM are both ≤12, the parser can pick the wrong triple or swap fields.","evidence":["034.jpg true date 09/03/2018 → emitted 2018-08-09 (month/day swapped)"]},{"id":"rc_number_token_fragility","summary":"The amount regex requires clean 'd+\\.dd' and does not repair OCR digit-letter confusions inside numeric tokens (e.g. '15.u00', '88.1' truncation, '5.09' vs '5.00'). There is no second-pass OCR on the total region, no whitelist OCR ('-c tessedit_char_whitelist=0123456789.,RM'), and no multi-pass preprocessing fallback when the top candidate line yields no parseable number.","evidence":["011.jpg prior OCR 'TOTAL 15.u00' would silently fail without a repair pass","064.jpg 'Total Gross C RM 88.1' truncated to 88.10"]},{"id":"rc_image_listing_filter","summary":"Although sorting is lexicographic, there is no explicit guarantee in the skill that the writer uses exactly the directory listing (hidden files, non-image files, or alternate extensions could change row count); the strict-schema skill mentions this but image-ocr does not enforce it.","evidence":["xlsx skill checklist calls for 'row count equals number of inputs' but image-ocr iter_images rule is only an example, not required"]}],"skill_defects":[{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Structured Field Extraction section defines priority tiers and exclusions but (a) chooses the LAST matching line within a tier without section-awareness, (b) does not list a 'GST/TAX SUMMARY section suppression' rule, (c) does not describe preference for post-rounding/grand-total variants when multiple totals coexist, and (d) does not require a second-pass OCR / numeric-whitelist retry when the selected keyword line yields no parseable number."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Keyword regexes are too literal. They should tolerate common OCR corruptions: missing space ('GrandTotal'), 'RM' misread as 'RN'/'Ri'/'RH', 'Total' with stray punctuation, and concatenated 'Total:RM'. The skill should prescribe a normalization pass (collapse spaces, RM-variant canonicalization) before keyword matching."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"DATE_PATTERNS list prefers the first regex that matches anywhere in the text and does not: (a) prefer tokens on a line containing 'Date', (b) disambiguate DD/MM vs MM/DD using year position and known receipt locale, (c) validate against calendar bounds beyond simple 1-31/1-12. Needs an explicit 'anchor on Date: label when present, then fall back to first plausible token' rule."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"process_receipt returns None on exception but does not require the amount-extraction path to also retry with (i) preprocessing variants and (ii) a Tesseract numeric whitelist pass on the keyword line's bounding region. A single rule 'iterate files via sorted(Path(dir).iterdir()) filtered to IMG_EXT, and let row order follow iteration order' would remove a class of row-count/order bugs."},{"skill":"openai-vision","defect":"Not used in this run, but the skill does not mention it as a fallback OCR engine for receipts where Tesseract produces unrecoverable digit corruption (e.g. '15.u00', truncated '88.1'). A cross-skill note in image-ocr pointing to openai-vision for a last-resort structured extraction would help generalize."}],"repair_recommendations":[{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"In Structured Field Extraction, replace 'take the match' with an explicit selection policy: (1) iterate priority tiers high→low; (2) within each tier, collect ALL candidate lines; (3) drop any candidate that appears after a line matching /GST\\s*SUMMARY|TAX\\s*SUMMARY|SST\\s*SUMMARY/i; (4) among remaining candidates prefer, in order, lines matching /ROUND(ED|ING)|AFTER\\s*ADJ|GRAND/i, then the LAST remaining candidate; (5) if the chosen line has no parseable number, fall through to the two-line fallback, then to the next-best candidate, then to the next tier."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Add a 'Pre-normalization' subsection: before keyword/number matching, apply text normalizations — collapse runs of whitespace, insert a space between a lowercase letter and an uppercase letter ('GrandTotal'→'Grand Total'), replace standalone 'RN','RH','Ri','PM' tokens adjacent to amounts with 'RM', and strip stray punctuation around 'TOTAL'/'AMOUNT'. Show the exact regex substitutions."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Extend NUM_RE handling with a repair step that, on the selected keyword line only, substitutes common OCR confusions inside numeric tokens (O/o→0, l/I→1, S→5, B→8, u→0) and re-tries parsing; document this as 'numeric-token repair applied only when the line already matched a total keyword'."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Make multi_pass_ocr an explicit fallback inside process_receipt: if extract_total(text) is None OR extract_date(text) is None, re-run with multi_pass_ocr output and merge results; document that this is bounded (one extra pass) to avoid runaway cost."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Rewrite extract_date to: (1) first search lines containing /DATE|TARIKH/i for a date token; (2) prefer 4-digit-year patterns over 2-digit; (3) when both DD/MM and MM/DD parses are valid, prefer DD/MM only if the surrounding receipt uses metric/Malay conventions (default DD/MM for RM receipts), else the earliest plausible reading-order token; (4) always validate with datetime.strptime and reject impossible dates."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Add a 'Null contract' subsection stating that process_receipt MUST return Python None (never '', 'None', 'NaN') for any field it cannot extract, and that callers writing to tabular outputs must propagate None unchanged."},{"skill":"xlsx","change":"In Strict-Schema Outputs → Canonical Pattern, add explicit rules: (a) build rows by iterating sorted(Path(dir).iterdir()) filtered to the task's extension set; (b) never call .fillna on the extracted fields; (c) after writing, re-read with pandas and assert that every unparsed cell is pd.isna, not ''; (d) assert sheet names and column order exactly match the task spec."},{"skill":"xlsx","change":"In the Pitfalls list, add: 'Writing empty string for missing extractions — breaks null contracts.
